about: ORI's own paraphrases of the effect of each Chapter 6 rule unit (2021 VRC = 2021 IRC as amended by 13VAC5-63-210). Summaries in ORI's words, not code text and not interpretations; read the linked official source. Bare numeric thresholds are kept where a rule needs them. Titles live in catalogue_ch06.py and are ORI descriptions, not ICC section headings. Policy: docs/CITATION-POLICY.md.
license: CC0-1.0 (ORI text only; no ICC text is included)

paraphrases.R601.1: Chapter 6 governs how above-grade walls are built: materials, framing, bracing and the window and door units set in them.
paraphrases.R601.2: Walls must be built from the materials and by the methods the chapter allows, so that they carry the loads the code assigns to them.
paraphrases.R601.2.1: A thick or soft floor finish under a wall can let it settle; the wall must still bear properly on the structure below.
paraphrases.R602.1: Lumber and panel products used in walls need a grade stamp from an accredited agency, or a certificate of inspection in its place.
paraphrases.R602.1.1: Sawn wall lumber must show its grade through an accredited grading mark or an equivalent certificate.
paraphrases.R602.1.2: Finger-jointed lumber may be used like solid lumber of the same grade, with limits on where heat-resistant adhesive is needed.
paraphrases.R602.1.3: Glulam members must be made and marked to the referenced laminated-timber standards.
paraphrases.R602.1.4: Log members used structurally must be graded to the referenced log standard.
paraphrases.R602.1.5: Engineered lumber such as LVL or PSL must meet its referenced standard and be used within its listing.
paraphrases.R602.1.6: Cross-laminated timber panels must be made to the referenced standard.
paraphrases.R602.1.7: Engineered rim boards must meet their referenced standard and be marked.
paraphrases.R602.1.8: Plywood and OSB used in walls must be made to the referenced panel standards and carry identifying marks.
paraphrases.R602.1.9: Particleboard used in walls must meet its referenced standard and be marked.
paraphrases.R602.1.10: Fiberboard sheathing must meet its referenced standard.
paraphrases.R602.2: Studs must be of at least the minimum grade the code sets; lower utility grades are allowed only in limited cases.
paraphrases.R602.3: Wall members and sheathing must be fastened as the code's fastener schedules set out, and framed per the typical framing figures.
paraphrases.R602.3.1|stud spacing: Stud size and on-center spacing must suit what the wall carries (roof only, one floor, two floors) per the stud table; ORI encodes only the few values its tests need, pending an owner decision on table data.
paraphrases.R602.3.1|stud height: Bearing studs have a limit on height between points of lateral support; taller walls need the listed alternative or an engineered design.
paraphrases.R602.3.1|exceptions: Utility-grade studs and taller studs are allowed under listed conditions that a reviewer must confirm.
paraphrases.R602.3.2|plate count: Bearing and exterior walls need two top plates, unless a single plate is tied at joints and corners and members bear over studs.
paraphrases.R602.3.2|splice offset: End joints in the two top plates must be staggered by a minimum distance and the lap fastened as the schedule sets out.
paraphrases.R602.3.3: Joists, trusses and rafters should land over the studs below, within a small allowed offset, unless the plate is sized to span the offset.
paraphrases.R602.3.4: Studs need a bottom plate at least as wide as the studs, bearing fully on the support below.
paraphrases.R602.3.5: Where wind uplift is high, the load path through braced wall panels must be completed with listed connectors or sheathing.
paraphrases.R602.4: Interior walls that carry loads are framed to the same rules as exterior walls.
paraphrases.R602.5: Interior walls that carry no load may use lighter framing and a single top plate, within the limits set.
paraphrases.R602.6|bored holes: Holes drilled through studs are limited in diameter relative to stud depth and must stay a minimum distance from the edges; larger holes need doubled studs.
paraphrases.R602.6|notches: Notches cut into studs are limited to a fraction of stud depth, with a smaller limit in bearing and exterior walls than in nonbearing walls.
paraphrases.R602.6.1: Where piping or ducts cut most of the top plate width, a metal tie must bridge the cut and be nailed on each side.
paraphrases.R602.7: Headers over openings must be sized for the span and load per the header tables, or engineered.
paraphrases.R602.7.1: Single-member headers are allowed where the table permits, with the stated framing at the top.
paraphrases.R602.7.2: Rim boards may serve as headers above openings within the stated limits.
paraphrases.R602.7.3: Box headers built from wood structural panels and lumber may be used within the stated spans and loads.
paraphrases.R602.7.4: Openings in nonbearing walls may use a flat member or a single top plate as the header.
paraphrases.R602.7.5: Headers bear on jack studs or approved hangers, and a minimum number of full-height studs is needed at each end depending on span and wind.
paraphrases.R602.8: Concealed wall cavities must be fireblocked as Section R302.11 requires.
paraphrases.R602.9: Short walls between foundation and first floor must be framed with studs at least as large as those above, and braced; tall ones count as a story.
paraphrases.R602.10: Walls must be braced against lateral loads by R602.10 or the alternative path; Virginia lets the building official require braced wall lines on the drawings with supporting analysis.
paraphrases.R602.10.1: Each story is divided into braced wall lines along which bracing is provided.
paraphrases.R602.10.1.1: A braced wall line's length is measured between its end lines as the code describes.
paraphrases.R602.10.1.2: Wall segments may be offset from a braced wall line by a limited distance and still count toward it.
paraphrases.R602.10.1.3: Braced wall lines must not be farther apart than the spacing limit for the wind or seismic condition.
paraphrases.R602.10.1.4: Short angled walls at corners may be treated as part of an adjacent braced wall line.
paraphrases.R602.10.2: Braced wall panels must sit along braced wall lines and be placed per the location rules.
paraphrases.R602.10.2.1: Braced wall panels need a continuous uplift path where design wind is high.
paraphrases.R602.10.2.2: Panels must begin within a set distance of each end of a braced wall line and be spaced within set limits.
paraphrases.R602.10.2.3: Each braced wall line needs at least a minimum number of panels.
paraphrases.R602.10.3: The total bracing along each line must at least equal the length the wind and seismic tables require after adjustment factors.
paraphrases.R602.10.4: Panels must use one of the listed bracing methods built as described.
paraphrases.R602.10.4.1: Bracing methods may be mixed only in the ways allowed.
paraphrases.R602.10.4.2: Continuously sheathed methods need sheathing over all wall areas, including above and below openings.
paraphrases.R602.10.4.3: Some bracing methods need interior gypsum finish, or a length increase where it is omitted.
paraphrases.R602.10.4.4: Vertical panel joints land on studs and horizontal joints need blocking, except where the method permits otherwise.
paraphrases.R602.10.5: Each panel must meet the minimum length for its method and wall height.
paraphrases.R602.10.5.1: The length a panel contributes depends on its method and dimensions.
paraphrases.R602.10.5.2: Panels shorter than the minimum may earn partial credit as the code allows.
paraphrases.R602.10.6: Alternate, portal-frame and similar methods must be built to their own detailed requirements.
paraphrases.R602.10.7: Continuously sheathed braced wall lines need specific end conditions.
paraphrases.R602.10.8: Braced panels must be connected to the floor or roof above and below so loads transfer.
paraphrases.R602.10.9: Braced panels must be supported on continuous foundations or on stem walls built as shown; Virginia adds an adhesive-anchor option for masonry stem walls.
paraphrases.R602.10.10: Cripple walls need their own bracing per the stated rules.
paraphrases.R602.10.11: Higher seismic categories add bracing limits; most Virginia sites are outside those categories.
paraphrases.R602.11: Walls are anchored to the foundation per the foundation anchorage rules, with extra measures in high seismic areas.
paraphrases.R602.12: Model code: a simplified bracing path for limited buildings. Virginia replaces it with practical wall bracing for low seismic categories, where the official may require bracing on the drawings with analysis.
paraphrases.R602.12.1: Virginia practical bracing: panels may be wood structural panel (at least 7/16 in), structural fiberboard (at least 1/2 in) or, on interior walls only, gypsum board (at least 1/2 in); exterior walls are fully sheathed.
paraphrases.R602.12.2|exterior panel length: Virginia practical bracing: an outside-wall panel needs a minimum length that grows with wall height and with how tall the neighbouring door or window is; where two neighbours differ, use the taller one.
paraphrases.R602.12.2|interior panel length: Virginia practical bracing: an interior panel sheathed on one side must be at least 48 in long; a panel sheathed both sides counts as two.
paraphrases.R602.12.2|panel construction: Virginia practical bracing: panels are full height; most exterior panels need interior gypsum finish unless the required length is increased by 1.40; joints land on studs or blocking.
paraphrases.R602.12.3: Virginia practical bracing: draw rectangles around the building; no side may exceed 80 ft and the long side may be at most 3 times the short side.
paraphrases.R602.12.4: Virginia practical bracing: each rectangle side needs a required length of bracing from the bracing table, with adjustment factors.
paraphrases.R602.12.4.1: Virginia practical bracing: panels count toward the parallel rectangle side they sit on or face; interior panels count only within 4 ft of that side.
paraphrases.R602.12.4.2: Virginia practical bracing: add up the panels credited to a rectangle side and compare with that side's required total; outside-wall panels earn their whole length, interior ones half.
paraphrases.R602.12.4.3: Virginia practical bracing: panels on a shared wall of skewed rectangles may be assigned to either side as allowed.
paraphrases.R602.12.5: Virginia practical bracing: cripple walls up to 48 in use the normal required length; taller cripple walls and walk-out basement walls use the table with the story counted.
paraphrases.R602.12.6|corner distance: Virginia practical bracing: a panel edge must be within 12 ft of every building or rectangle corner.
paraphrases.R602.12.6|panel gap: Virginia practical bracing: adjacent panel edges may be at most 20 ft apart.
paraphrases.R602.12.6|segment rule: Virginia practical bracing: exterior wall segments longer than 8 ft need at least one panel; shorter segments may have none.
paraphrases.R602.12.6.1: Virginia practical bracing: where a wall is balloon framed, every story beside it gets panels on both faces of that wall.
paraphrases.R602.12.7: Virginia practical bracing: panels connect to other structure as R602.10.8 requires.
paraphrases.R602.12.8: Virginia practical bracing: panels are supported as R602.10.9 requires.
paraphrases.R603: Cold-formed steel wall framing must stay within the prescriptive limits on building size, wind and snow, and follow the stud, bracing and header rules, or be engineered.
paraphrases.R604: Wood structural panel sheathing must be of the grade and thickness the span tables permit for the stud spacing.
paraphrases.R605: Particleboard wall sheathing must be of the grade and thickness allowed for the stud spacing.
paraphrases.R606: Masonry walls must meet the general rules on materials, thickness, bonding, mortar, grout, lintels and anchorage.
paraphrases.R607: Glass block panels must stay within their size and support limits and be built as described.
paraphrases.R608: Exterior concrete walls must stay within the prescriptive limits or be engineered, with the stated reinforcement and connections.
paraphrases.R609: Exterior windows and doors, including garage doors, must meet their design pressure ratings and carry labels from testing.
paraphrases.R610: Structural insulated panel walls must stay within the stated building limits and be built and connected as described.
